refinements.outcome: E24 isolates Finance employee compensation, customer-facing booking markup, earned commission, customer-debt collection accountability and self/manager-scoped views into five story boundaries.
refinements.context: Finance owns salary, policy and earning ledger; Booking owns attribution and frozen guest-facing markup; User owns staff identity/branch links. Current Finance migrations V1–V4 have settlement and rules but no employee salary or commission tables. Only S01 has detailed leaf refinement in this wave.

refinements.outcome: S01 versions restricted effective-dated salary/compensation in Finance, uses authenticated User employment identity, and shows only authorized self/manager views without a salary copy in Booking or UI.
refinements.context: A salary record is confidential employee financial data; an employee may view their own approved compensation, while a manager sees only assigned authorized scope. Compensation amounts and policy activation require finance approval.

refinements.summary: [VS-E24-S01-ST01] Persist effective-dated salary and compensation profiles in Finance
refinements.outcome: Finance stores one auditable, nonoverlapping approved compensation version per employee and organization, including base salary, currency, pay period and approval provenance.
refinements.context: service_finance currently has V1–V4 for payables, settlement and rule catalogue; no employee salary/profile table or approved default is present.
inScope: Add Finance-owned migration/profile model with employee subject reference, organization/site scope, base salary minor units, currency, monthly pay period, validFrom/validTo, lifecycle status, maker/checker IDs and audit history.
Provide draft, simulate, approve/publish, supersede and self/authorized-manager read APIs with expected revision, stable errors, write idempotency and denied overlap.
Resolve employee and branch scope from User purpose-bound link and reject inactive staff, self-approval, cross-branch access and incomplete policy approval.
outOfScope: Tax, insurance, net payroll calculation, bank payout, or duplicate salary table in Booking/User.

artifacts: employee compensation migration and immutable versions
restricted Finance read/write and maker-checker flow

interfaces: Version restricted Finance REST or GraphQL contract for compensation draft/approve/get with policy revision, effective interval and response-field filtering.
dataOwnership: Finance owns approved compensation versions and salary audit; User supplies employment/branch identity, Booking owns booking attribution only.
stateMachine: DRAFT -> SUBMITTED -> APPROVED -> ACTIVE -> SUPERSEDED; REJECTED is terminal. An active interval is unique per employee/organization/currency/pay-period.

dataPartitions: Employee SELF only for the authenticated staff subject; manager FINANCE access is constrained to the authorized organization/site/branch; SYSTEM access is purpose-bound with verified caller; no cross-employee or cross-branch salary lookup.
fieldGroups: FINANCIAL salary requires explicit self/manager field grant; INTERNAL_AUDIT approval/history requires separate grant; SUMMARY excludes salary amount.

failureSemantics: Missing employment link, active approved compensation policy, field grant or authoritative staff identity fails closed; no zero-salary or default commission is inferred.
Conflict, stale source revision, invalid compensation interval, denied partition and dependency outage return distinct stable reasons without exposing salary or employee PII.
Never log unredacted salary, private employee documents, bank details, JWT or cross-staff revenue; audit only authorized fingerprints.
idempotencyConcurrency: Externally retried mutation uses scoped idempotency key and fingerprint with expected revision; concurrent interval overlap or actor reassignment is rejected.
Historical effective-dated salary is immutable; a correction creates a new superseding revision, not an update to closed payroll history.
Source events use outbox/inbox event ID and aggregate revision so duplicates/reorder cannot create a second compensation fact.

acceptanceCriteria.then: change is rejected with a stable reason without revealing employee salary

acceptanceCriteria.given: same approval retries or older correction arrives
acceptanceCriteria.then: one active interval and one audit revision survive with historical salary unchanged
